overview.description: A gBlock is a synthetic DNA strand designed for insertion. Good design front-loads success: pick compatible cut sites, include the transcription/translation machinery, and plan affinity tags now because they're painful to add later.
objectives: design an insert with correct restriction/assembly sites
add affinity and cleavage tags thoughtfully
apply codon optimisation for your host

instructions.title: Define the construct
instructions.description: Lay out promoter, RBS, start/stop codons, your gene, and any tags in the correct frame.

instructions.title: Add compatible sites
instructions.description: Include restriction sites (or assembly overhangs) that match your chosen backbone and won't cut internally.

instructions.title: Codon-optimise
instructions.description: Optimise codons for your host to boost expression, then order the synthesised fragment.

submission.description: Design a complete insert in your viewer, with annotated sites and tags, ready to order. Export the sequence.
